themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 16 THIS WEEK, a 125% increase from the 7.1-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.51), suggesting a sudden environmental or building-system failure affecting multiple households in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 16 indoor air quality complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 7.1-complaint weekly baseline (125% spike)
Z-score of 6.51 indicates statistically extreme deviation from 8-week pattern
No explanatory news coverage or external events identified in local reporting
Timing coincides with recent deadly Inwood blaze (May 14) — potential for related fire-damage air contamination
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents across multiple buildings to identify common air quality issue (mold, gas leak, ventilation failure, post-fire smoke)
Contact NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene and buildings department to investigate source and scope of complaints
Investigate whether post-fire cleanup efforts in Inwood may be contributing to air quality degradation in surrounding buildings

themes_detail.label: Safety Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Safety complaints jumped to 27 LAST WEEK, a 112% increase from the 12.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.96), indicating a sudden deterioration in perceived or actual public safety across the district.
evidence: 27 safety complaints last week vs. 12.8-complaint weekly baseline (112% spike)
Z-score of 3.96 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Recent deadly residential fire in Inwood (May 14, reported by The City) may have elevated resident concern about structural safety and enforcement
Correlates with encampment complaints spike (21 complaints 2 weeks ago, up 409%), suggesting homelessness-related safety concerns may be driving surge
reporting_angles: Analyze 311 complaint text to categorize safety concerns (assault, theft, unsupervised encampments, fire hazards, blocked exits)
Interview residents and 108th Precinct to understand specific safety incidents or patterns driving the spike
Cross-reference with recent deadly fire story — have enforcement actions decreased or has community trust eroded post-incident?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Growth Accelerates
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 21 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 409% increase from the 4.1-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.01), marking a sharp expansion of homeless encampments in public spaces across Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 21 encampment complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.1-complaint weekly baseline (409% spike)
Z-score of 5.01 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Correlates with simultaneous park-rules violations spike (6 last week vs. 1.9 baseline, +220%)
Correlates with safety complaints surge (27 last week), suggesting encampment-related safety concerns
No community board or budget request data available to contextualize historical funding for outreach
reporting_angles: Map locations of the 21 encampment complaints to identify which parks, streets, or public spaces are most affected
Interview residents, Parks Department, and Homeless Services to understand root cause of sudden spike and whether prior outreach capacity has been reduced
Talk to unhoused individuals to understand why Washington Heights/Inwood has become a concentration point (shelter capacity, services availability, enforcement patterns)

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Flood District
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints exploded to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1500% spike from the 0.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.66, the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset), suggesting either a sudden bike-sharing system failure or coordinated abandonment event.
evidence: 4 abandoned bike complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2-complaint weekly baseline (1500% spike)
Z-score of 8.66 is the single highest anomaly across all complaint categories analyzed
Pattern suggests discrete event rather than gradual trend (baseline almost zero, sudden spike)
No external news coverage identified explaining event
reporting_angles: Contact Citi Bike and other bike-share operators to determine if there was a system outage, theft ring, or redistribution event 2 weeks ago
Visit identified locations of abandoned bikes to observe current conditions and interview nearby residents
Query 311 complaint text for specific locations and descriptions to determine if bikes are Citi Bike-branded or personal bikes

themes_detail.label: Sanitation System Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Sanitation worker or vehicle complaints spiked to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 700% increase from the 0.5-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.95), indicating possible failures in garbage collection or street-sweeping services across the district.
evidence: 4 sanitation worker/vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5-complaint weekly baseline (700% spike)
Z-score of 4.95 indicates high statistical significance
Correlates with broader unsanitary condition complaints (1,332 total over 90 days, suggesting systemic issues)
No corroborating news coverage identified
reporting_angles: Contact Department of Sanitation to determine if there were staffing shortages, truck breakdowns, or route changes 2 weeks ago
Interview residents and local business owners about garbage collection reliability and street cleanliness
Observe actual sanitation service conditions on streets cited in complaints
